proposals: FSSAI should publish a clarification stating whether PLA and other bio-based polyesters fall within the August 2026 ban on synthetic polymers in pan masala packaging, so that a ban that names polyester is reconciled with the January 2026 consultation that named PLA as the preferred sachet material.

The Environment Ministry should notify its revised definition of bioplastics, and BIS should then publish the testing protocol for bioplastic sachets with a target date, so that the certification pathway left open in January 2026 has a public end point.

The Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser should publish the minutes of its follow-up meeting and the draft SOP for bioplastic sachets, with the results of material samples sent to CIPET, so that the process’s status after FSSAI’s ban can be checked.

CBIC should require PLA to be declared under HSN 39077000 rather than broader blended-polymer lines, so that India’s PLA import bill — recorded at $10.19 million against a reported 17% share of global PLA imports — can be measured before domestic supply arrives.

The Department of Biotechnology should publish whether, and by when, the BioE3 Policy’s proposed PLI extension to bioplastics will be notified, so that mills considering a PLA line know whether the incentive is policy direction or money on the table.
